```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// ---- Data load -----------------------------------------------------------
// typed:true would coerce countyfips ("08000") to a number and destroy the
// leading zero, so we load untyped and auto-type every column except that one.
raw = FileAttachment("output/netmig-comparison.csv").csv()
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
data = raw.map((d) => {
  const fips = d.countyfips;
  const t = d3.autoType(d);
  t.countyfips = fips;
  return t;
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// age_group is age at the END of the period, in one of two groupings: "five"
// (eighteen five-year groups) or "broad" (0-17, 18-24, 25-44, 45-64, 65+).
// age_order gives display order within a grouping.
ageLevelsFor = (grouping) =>
  Array.from(
    d3.rollup(
      data.filter((d) => d.grouping === grouping),
      (v) => v[0].age_order,
      (d) => d.age_group
    ),
    ([g, o]) => ({ g, o })
  )
    .sort((a, b) => a.o - b.o)
    .map((d) => d.g)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
groupingOptions = new Map([
  ["Five-year groups", "five"],
  ["0-17, 18-24, 25-44, 45-64, 65+", "broad"]
])
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
countyOptions = {
  const others = Array.from(new Set(data.map((d) => d.county)))
    .filter((c) => c !== "Colorado")
    .sort();
  return ["Colorado", ...others];
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Chronological order drives every sort/legend/earliest-latest calc below.
periodOptions = ["1990-2000", "2000-2010", "2010-2020", "2020-2025"]
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
periodYears = {
  return {
    "1990-2000": { start: 1990, end: 2000 },
    "2000-2010": { start: 2000, end: 2010 },
    "2010-2020": { start: 2010, end: 2020 },
    "2020-2025": { start: 2020, end: 2025 }
  };
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Fixed period -> colour mapping so a period's colour never changes as the
// selection changes. Keeps SDO navy/orange for the two most-viewed periods.
periodColor = new Map([
  ["1990-2000", "#6B7280"],
  ["2000-2010", "#8B5FBF"],
  ["2010-2020", "#E3791C"],
  ["2020-2025", "#003E82"]
])
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Same swatch order Plot's "tableau10" scheme would assign, but held here as
// an explicit array so the SVG export can redraw the legend.
countyColors = d3.schemeTableau10
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
measureSlug = (key) => (key === "rate_per_1000" ? "rate" : "people")
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// ---- SVG export ----------------------------------------------------------
// Observable Plot returns a bare <svg>, or (whenever a colour legend is
// requested inline) a <figure> wrapping an <svg> plus an HTML legend div.
// PowerPoint needs a self-contained, explicitly-sized SVG: Plot's on-page
// look depends on a stylesheet class (currentColor fills/strokes) that does
// not travel with a downloaded file, and the HTML legend has to be redrawn
// as SVG shapes/text since it isn't part of the <svg> at all.
buildExportSvg = (chart, legend) => {
  // Plot returns a bare <svg> for a plain chart, but a <figure> wrapping the
  // legend (tiny per-swatch <svg> icons!) plus the real chart <svg> whenever
  // a colour legend is requested inline -- querySelector("svg") would grab
  // the first swatch icon instead of the chart, so pick the largest one.
  const root =
    chart.tagName === "svg"
      ? chart
      : Array.from(chart.querySelectorAll("svg")).reduce((best, s) => {
          const area = (r) => r.width * r.height;
          if (!best) return s;
          return area(s.getBoundingClientRect()) > area(best.getBoundingClientRect()) ? s : best;
        }, null);
  if (!root) return null;
  const svg = root.cloneNode(true);

  // Inline every element's *computed* fill/stroke/font so nothing depends
  // on a CSS class that won't be present when the file is opened elsewhere.
  const origEls = root.querySelectorAll("*");
  const cloneEls = svg.querySelectorAll("*");
  origEls.forEach((o, i) => {
    const c = cloneEls[i];
    if (!c) return;
    const cs = getComputedStyle(o);
    if (cs.fill && cs.fill !== "none") c.setAttribute("fill", cs.fill);
    if (cs.stroke && cs.stroke !== "none" && cs.stroke !== "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)") {
      c.setAttribute("stroke", cs.stroke);
    }
    if (o.tagName === "text" || o.tagName === "tspan") {
      c.setAttribute("font-family", cs.fontFamily);
      c.setAttribute("font-size", cs.fontSize);
    }
  });

  const w = +(root.getAttribute("width") ?? root.clientWidth ?? 800);
  const h = +(root.getAttribute("height") ?? root.clientHeight ?? 400);
  svg.setAttribute("width", w);
  svg.setAttribute("height", h);
  svg.setAttribute("viewBox", root.getAttribute("viewBox") ?? `0 0 ${w} ${h}`);
  svg.setAttribute("xmlns", "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg");

  if (legend && legend.domain.length) {
    const itemW = 150;
    const rowH = 20;
    const perRow = Math.max(1, Math.floor(w / itemW));
    const rows = Math.ceil(legend.domain.length / perRow);
    const legendH = 10 + rows * rowH;
    svg.setAttribute("height", h + legendH);
    svg.setAttribute("viewBox", `0 0 ${w} ${h + legendH}`);
    const wrapper = document.createElementNS("http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", "g");
    wrapper.setAttribute("transform", `translate(0, ${legendH})`);
    while (svg.firstChild) wrapper.appendChild(svg.firstChild);
    svg.appendChild(wrapper);
    legend.domain.forEach((label, i) => {
      const col = i % perRow;
      const row = Math.floor(i / perRow);
      const x = 6 + col * itemW;
      const y = 6 + row * rowH;
      const rect = document.createElementNS("http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", "rect");
      rect.setAttribute("x", x);
      rect.setAttribute("y", y);
      rect.setAttribute("width", 11);
      rect.setAttribute("height", 11);
      rect.setAttribute("fill", legend.range[i % legend.range.length]);
      svg.appendChild(rect);
      const text = document.createElementNS("http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", "text");
      text.setAttribute("x", x + 15);
      text.setAttribute("y", y + 9.5);
      text.setAttribute("font-size", "11px");
      text.setAttribute("font-family", "Arial, sans-serif");
      text.setAttribute("fill", "#212529");
      text.textContent = label;
      svg.appendChild(text);
    });
  }

  return svg;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
downloadChartSvg = (chart, filename, legend = null) => {
  const svg = buildExportSvg(chart, legend);
  if (!svg) return;
  const xml = new XMLSerializer().serializeToString(svg);
  const blob = new Blob([xml], { type: "image/svg+xml;charset=utf-8" });
  const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
  const a = document.createElement("a");
  a.href = url;
  a.download = filename;
  document.body.appendChild(a);
  a.click();
  a.remove();
  setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 1000);
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
svgDownloadButton = (chart, filename, legend = null) => {
  const btn = html`<button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary dl-button">⬇ Download SVG</button>`;
  btn.onclick = () => downloadChartSvg(chart, filename, legend);
  return btn;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// One place that defines both first-class measures. Every chart, KPI, and
// table column reads formatting/labels from here so switching the selector
// can never leave a stale label or number format behind.
measures = {
  const rate_per_1000 = {
    key: "rate_per_1000",
    label: "Annual net migration rate (per 1,000 people)",
    short: "Rate per 1,000",
    axis: "Net migration rate (annual, per 1,000)",
    fmt: (v) => (v < 0 ? "−" : "+") + d3.format(",.1f")(Math.abs(v)) + " per 1,000",
    fmtShort: (v) => (v < 0 ? "−" : "+") + d3.format(",.1f")(Math.abs(v)),
    tickFormat: (v) => d3.format("+,.0f")(v)
  };
  const netmig_annual = {
    key: "netmig_annual",
    label: "Annual net migration (people per year)",
    short: "People per year",
    axis: "Net migration (people per year)",
    fmt: (v) => (v < 0 ? "−" : "+") + d3.format(",.0f")(Math.abs(v)) + "/yr",
    fmtShort: (v) => (v < 0 ? "−" : "+") + d3.format(",.0f")(Math.abs(v)),
    tickFormat: (v) => d3.format("+,")(v)
  };
  return { rate_per_1000, netmig_annual };
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// The same people's ages at the START of the period: the end-of-period group
// shifted back by the period's length. Ages below zero were born during it.
originLabel = (d) => {
  const [lo, hiText] = d.age_group.replace("+", "-").split("-");
  const sLo = +lo - d.years;
  if (hiText === "") return sLo < 0 ? "Born during period or 0+" : `${sLo}+`;
  const sHi = +hiText - d.years;
  if (sHi < 0) return "Born during period";
  if (sLo < 0) return `Born during period or 0-${sHi}`;
  return `${sLo}-${sHi}`;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
cohortLabel = (d) => {
  const py = periodYears[d.period];
  const origin = originLabel(d);
  const originText = origin === "Born during period"
    ? "Born during the period"
    : `${origin} in ${py.start}`;
  return `${originText} → ${d.age_group} in ${py.end}`;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Shown under a chart when any of its rows carries a caveat (the 2000
// Broomfield boundary change in 1990-2000).
caveatNote = (rows) => {
  const notes = Array.from(new Set(rows.map((d) => d.caveat).filter(Boolean)));
  if (!notes.length) return html``;
  const areas = Array.from(new Set(rows.filter((d) => d.caveat).map((d) => d.county))).join(", ");
  return html`<div class="control-hint">⚠ ${areas}, 1990-2000: ${notes.join(" ")}</div>`;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Aggregating rate_per_1000 by summing rows would be wrong (it's a ratio);
// the correct aggregate rate is total annual net migration over total mean
// population. This is used anywhere a KPI sums across age groups.
aggregateMeasure = (rows, measureKey) => {
  const annual = d3.sum(rows, (d) => d.netmig_annual);
  const pop = d3.sum(rows, (d) => d.mean_pop);
  return measureKey === "rate_per_1000" ? (pop > 0 ? (annual / pop) * 1000 : 0) : annual;
}
```

:::

# Compare periods

## {.sidebar}

Follow one area across the selected periods to see how its age profile of
net migration shifted.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof area_p = Inputs.select(countyOptions, { label: "Area", value: "Colorado" })
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof periods_p = Inputs.checkbox(periodOptions, { label: "Periods", value: periodOptions })
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof sex_p = Inputs.radio(["Total", "Male", "Female"], { label: "Sex", value: "Total" })
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof grouping_p = Inputs.radio(groupingOptions, { label: "Age groups", value: "five" })
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof measure_p = Inputs.radio(
  new Map([
    ["Rate per 1,000 (annual)", "rate_per_1000"],
    ["People per year (annual)", "netmig_annual"]
  ]),
  { label: "Measure", value: "rate_per_1000" }
)
```

<div class="control-hint">Rates let you compare areas of different sizes.</div>

::: {.callout-note}
Age groups are age at the **end** of the period. A bar labeled "25-29" in
2020-2025 follows the people who were 20-24 in 2020. Hover any mark to see
where that cohort started.
:::

::: {.hidden}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Chronological order regardless of the order the checkboxes report back in;
// fall back to every period if the user unchecks all of them.
selectedPeriods_p = {
  const sel = periodOptions.filter((p) => periods_p.includes(p));
  return sel.length ? sel : periodOptions;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
earliestPeriod_p = selectedPeriods_p[0]
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
latestPeriod_p = selectedPeriods_p[selectedPeriods_p.length - 1]
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
rows_p = data.filter(
  (d) =>
    d.grouping === grouping_p &&
    d.county === area_p &&
    d.sex_label === sex_p &&
    selectedPeriods_p.includes(d.period)
)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
byPeriod_p = d3.group(rows_p, (d) => d.period)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
valEarliest_p = aggregateMeasure(byPeriod_p.get(earliestPeriod_p) ?? [], measure_p)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
valLatest_p = aggregateMeasure(byPeriod_p.get(latestPeriod_p) ?? [], measure_p)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
peakRow_p = (byPeriod_p.get(latestPeriod_p) ?? [])
  .reduce((a, b) => (b[measure_p] > a[measure_p] ? b : a))
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Earliest vs. latest of the *selected* periods -- with only two selected
// this is exactly the old two-period comparison; with more it summarizes
// the full span while the grouped-bar chart above shows every period.
shiftRows_p = Array.from(
  d3.group(rows_p.filter((d) => d.period === earliestPeriod_p || d.period === latestPeriod_p), (d) => d.age_group),
  ([age_group, arr]) => {
    const r1 = arr.find((d) => d.period === earliestPeriod_p);
    const r2 = arr.find((d) => d.period === latestPeriod_p);
    return {
      age_group,
      age_order: r1.age_order,
      v1: r1[measure_p],
      v2: r2[measure_p],
      diff: r2[measure_p] - r1[measure_p]
    };
  }
).sort((a, b) => a.age_order - b.age_order)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
biggestShift_p = shiftRows_p.reduce((a, b) => (Math.abs(b.diff) > Math.abs(a.diff) ? b : a))
```

:::

```{ojs}
chart_p2 = Plot.plot({
  width,
  height: 340,
  marginLeft: 55,
  y: { domain: ageLevelsFor(grouping_p), label: null },
  x: {
    label: `Change in ${measures[measure_p].short.toLowerCase()}`,

    grid: true
  },
  marks: [
    Plot.ruleX([0]),
    Plot.barX(shiftRows_p, {
      x: "diff",
      y: "age_group",
      fill: (d) => (d.diff >= 0 ? "#003E82" : "#E3791C"),
      title: (d) =>
        `${d.age_group}: ${measures[measure_p].fmtShort(d.v1)} → ${measures[measure_p].fmtShort(d.v2)} (Δ ${measures[measure_p].fmt(d.diff)})`
    })
  ]
})
```

Navy = the rate rose between periods; orange = it fell (or turned negative).

# Compare areas

## {.sidebar}

Pick one period and 2+ areas to compare their age profiles directly.
Colorado is always available as a statewide reference (shown dashed).

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof period_a = Inputs.select(periodOptions, { label: "Period", value: "2020-2025" })
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof counties_a = Inputs.select(countyOptions, {
  label: "Areas (ctrl/cmd-click for multiple)",
  multiple: 6,
  value: ["Colorado", "Denver", "Weld", "Boulder"]
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof sex_a = Inputs.radio(["Total", "Male", "Female"], { label: "Sex", value: "Total" })
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof grouping_a = Inputs.radio(groupingOptions, { label: "Age groups", value: "five" })
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof measure_a = Inputs.radio(
  new Map([
    ["Rate per 1,000 (annual)", "rate_per_1000"],
    ["People per year (annual)", "netmig_annual"]
  ]),
  { label: "Measure", value: "rate_per_1000" }
)
```

<div class="control-hint">Rates let you compare areas of different sizes.</div>

::: {.callout-note}
Age groups are age at the **end** of the selected period.
:::

::: {.hidden}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
rows_a = data.filter(
  (d) =>
    d.grouping === grouping_a &&
    d.period === period_a &&
    counties_a.includes(d.county) &&
    d.sex_label === sex_a
)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
spreadByAge_a = Array.from(d3.group(rows_a, (d) => d.age_group), ([age_group, arr]) => ({
  age_group,
  age_order: arr[0].age_order,
  spread: d3.max(arr, (d) => d[measure_a]) - d3.min(arr, (d) => d[measure_a])
}))
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
widest_a = spreadByAge_a.length
  ? spreadByAge_a.reduce((a, b) => (b.spread > a.spread ? b : a))
  : { age_group: "n/a", spread: 0 }
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// The young-adult group that carries most of Colorado's net migration.
statewideRef_a = data.find(
  (d) =>
    d.grouping === grouping_a &&
    d.county === "Colorado" &&
    d.period === period_a &&
    d.sex_label === sex_a &&
    d.age_group === (grouping_a === "five" ? "25-29" : "25-44")
)
```

      strokeWidth: 2,
      r: 3,
      title: (d) => `${d.county} — ${cohortLabel(d)}\n${measures[measure_a].fmt(d[measure_a])}`
    })
  ]
})

::: {.hidden}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// One row per county (08000 = Colorado), sex, estimate year (ending July 1 of
// `year`) and single year of age at the end of that year. Built by R/01 and
// summed and written by R/02, with deaths estimated from public data.
annualRaw = FileAttachment("output/netmig-annual-sya-2020-2025.csv").csv()
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
annual = annualRaw.map((d) => {
  const fips = d.countyfips;
  const t = d3.autoType(d);
  t.countyfips = fips;
  return t;
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
countyByFips = new Map(data.map((d) => [d.countyfips, d.county]))
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Lower bound and label of each age group, by grouping.
groupings = {
  return {
    broad: [
      { lo: 0, label: "0-17" },
      { lo: 18, label: "18-24" },
      { lo: 25, label: "25-44" },
      { lo: 45, label: "45-64" },
      { lo: 65, label: "65+" }
    ],
    five: d3.range(0, 90, 5).map((lo) => ({ lo, label: lo === 85 ? "85+" : `${lo}-${lo + 4}` }))
  };
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
groupLevels_c = groupings[grouping_c].map((g) => g.label)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// A one-year cohort that ends year `year` at age_end is (end - year) years
// older at the end of the span. Summing its annual rows gives its net
// migration over the whole span; rows are then gathered by age group.
// Used for the current span and for every saved span on the comparison tab.
spanRows = (start, end, areas) => {
  const years = end - start;
  const groups = groupings[grouping_c];
  const groupOf = (age) => groups.filter((g) => g.lo <= age).at(-1).label;
  const sexCode = { Male: 1, Female: 2 }[sex_c];
  const out = [];
  for (const area of areas) {
    const fips = [...countyByFips].find(([, name]) => name === area)?.[0];
    const sums = new Map(groups.map((g) => [g.label, { netmig: 0, py: 0, popStart: 0, popEnd: 0 }]));
    for (const d of annual) {
      if (d.countyfips !== fips || d.year <= start || d.year > end) continue;
      if (sexCode && d.sex !== sexCode) continue;
      const s = sums.get(groupOf(Math.min(d.age_end + (end - d.year), 100)));
      s.netmig += d.netmig;
      s.py += d.person_years;
      if (d.year === start + 1) s.popStart += d.pop_start;
      if (d.year === end) s.popEnd += d.pop_end;
    }
    groups.forEach((g, i) => {
      const s = sums.get(g.label);
      out.push({
        county: area,
        span: `${start}-${end}`,
        age_group: g.label,
        age_order: i + 1,
        pop_start: s.popStart,
        pop_end: s.popEnd,
        person_years: s.py,
        people_total: s.netmig,
        people_annual: s.netmig / years,
        rate_annual: s.py > 0 ? (s.netmig / s.py) * 1000 : 0,
        rate_total: s.py > 0 ? (s.netmig / s.py) * 1000 * years : 0
      });
    });
  }
  return out;
}
```

```{ojs}

```

  ).values()

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Four measures: rate or people, each as an annual average or a total over
// the span. The two annual ones reuse the definitions shared with the other
// pages.
measures_c = {
  const signed = (f) => (v) => (v < 0 ? "−" : "+") + d3.format(f)(Math.abs(v));
  const people_total = {
    label: "Net migration over the span (people)",
    short: "People, span total",
    axis: "Net migration over the span (people)",
    fmt: signed(",.0f"),
    fmtShort: signed(",.0f"),
    tickFormat: (v) => d3.format("+,")(v)
  };
  const rate_total = {
    label: "Net migration over the span (per 1,000 people)",
    short: "Rate per 1,000, span total",
    axis: "Net migration over the span (per 1,000)",
    fmt: (v) => signed(",.1f")(v) + " per 1,000",
    fmtShort: signed(",.1f"),
    tickFormat: (v) => d3.format("+,.0f")(v)
  };
  return {
    rate_annual: measures.rate_per_1000,
    people_annual: measures.netmig_annual,
    rate_total,
    people_total
  };
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// All-ages value for the first area. A rate is total net migration over total
// person-years, never a sum of group rates.
allAges_c = {
  const r = rows_c.filter((d) => d.county === firstArea_c);
  const nm = d3.sum(r, (d) => d.people_total);
  const py = d3.sum(r, (d) => d.person_years);
  const years = end_c - start_c;
  const rate = py > 0 ? (nm / py) * 1000 : 0;
  return { people_total: nm, people_annual: nm / years, rate_annual: rate, rate_total: rate * years };
}
```

# Methods

## Row

::: {.card title="What this dashboard shows"}

This dashboard compares Colorado's implied net migration by age across
**64 counties** and **four periods** (1990-2000, 2000-2010, 2010-2020, and
2020-2025), and for any span inside 2020-2025. Net migration is estimated as a
demographic residual: population change minus births plus deaths. Full
derivation, validation, and county-by-county narrative are in the companion
report: [netmig-by-age.html](netmig-by-age.html).

### How it is built

Every figure on every page comes from one set of results: net migration for
each county, sex, single year of age and year from July 1990 to July 2025,
using the State Demography Office's single-year population estimates. Adding
up the one-year results for the same people gives exactly their net migration
over a longer period, which is how the four periods, both age groupings and
the custom spans are all formed. All pages use the same method, so the
2020-2025 figures agree across them.

County deaths by age are confidential, and because the population figures are
public, net migration published by age would let anyone work them back out
if it were built from recorded deaths. Deaths are therefore **estimated from
public data**: Colorado death rates by age and sex from the NCHS life tables, adjusted by each
county's own age pattern of deaths in CDPHE's public 2025 county summary
reports, and scaled to the county's published death total for each year.
County totals across all ages are unaffected. Against recorded deaths, the
broad age groups differ by a median of 6 to 7 people per decade (about 0.3 per
1,000 a year); the largest differences are in the oldest groups of the largest
counties, and are biggest in the 1990s, when county mortality patterns
differed most from those of 2025.

### Reading the age groups

`age_group` is **age at the end of the period**, not the start. A bar or point
labeled `25-29` in the 2020-2025 period represents the people who were 20-24 in
2020 and turned 25-29 by 2025 -- the tooltip on any mark shows where that group
started. Two groupings are offered on every page: eighteen five-year groups
and five broad groups (0-17, 18-24, 25-44, 45-64, 65+).

### Choosing a measure

- **Annual net migration (people per year)** -- net migration over the period
  divided by its length. A headcount, affected by the size of the area.
- **Annual net migration rate (per 1,000 people)** -- the same annual figure
  per 1,000 of the group's average population (person-years divided by the
  period's length). The size-neutral measure, and the default.
- On the **Custom span** page, either can also be shown as a **total over the
  span**; a total rate is the annual rate times the number of years.

Annual figures are comparable across periods of different length; totals are
not.

### The headline pattern

The 25-29 age group traces Colorado's boom-bust migration history: an annual
rate of +38.7 per 1,000 in 1990-2000, roughly halving to +19.5 in 2000-2010,
recovering to +28.3 in 2010-2020, and +36.1 in 2020-2025. Older working ages
tell the opposite story: the 55-59 group ran positive in every earlier period
(+8.7 in 1990-2000, +1.2 in 2000-2010, +0.9 in 2010-2020) and turned negative
in 2020-2025 (-5.0). In the broad groups, 45-64 and 65+ were both positive in
the 1990s (+10.7 and +5.4 per 1,000) and are both negative in 2020-2025 (-4.0
and -3.6). Colorado used to draw people at nearly every age and now draws
mainly young adults.

### Caveats

- These are the migration implied by published population estimates, not an
  independent measurement.
- **Broomfield, 1990-2000.** Broomfield County was formed in 2001 from parts of
  Adams, Boulder, Jefferson and Weld. The population estimates record the
  transfer of its territory in estimate year 2000 as migration, so the
  1990-2000 figures for those five counties include it. Affected rows carry a
  note.
- Small counties can have age-specific rates moved noticeably by a handful of
  people.

:::
